controls.title: Database-enforced tenant isolation
controls.validation: PostgreSQL non-superuser RLS tests and pooled-connection reuse tests run in the CI postgres job; a meta-test fails the build if a Postgres-only test file is missing from that job.
controls.notes: Application scoping plus ORM guard plus PostgreSQL FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY (triple guard).

controls.title: Privileged MFA and sensitive-action step-up
controls.gap: Native MFA/WebAuthn/TOTP and step-up authentication are not implemented (audit 2026-09-05 SEC-007; owner decision on policy in docs/DECISIONS-NEEDED.md).
controls.validation: MFA enrollment/login/recovery + privileged-action step-up tests; cross-path auth bypass tests.
controls.notes: Reinforced by the Personal-Security-Checklist cycle. Prefer phishing-resistant WebAuthn/passkeys where practical; implement from OWASP/NIST, not from a checklist.

controls.title: Session reauthentication and inactivity policy
controls.gap: Server-side sessions are revocable and expire, but the default overall TTL is 24h and last_seen is not an inactivity timeout.
controls.validation: Policy tests for inactivity/reauthentication and risk events; token/session rotation tests.
controls.notes: Coordinate with SEC-AUTH-001 so UX/security semantics are designed once.

controls.title: Immutable GitHub Actions dependencies
controls.validation: Every `uses:` in every workflow is `owner/repo@<40-hex SHA> # vN`; the SHAs were verified against the upstream tags with `git ls-remote` on 2026-09-07; `scripts/check_github_action_pins.py` runs in the CI lint job and in the supply-chain workflow, and a repository test asserts the same plus a top-level read-only `permissions:` block on every workflow and `persist-credentials: false` on every checkout — with one named exception, `ci.yml`'s `vr-baselines`, which publishes baselines to the dispatching branch (never main) and keeps `contents: write` for itself.
controls.notes: Release workflow has packages:write (the reason this was P1). Dependabot's github-actions ecosystem keeps the pinned SHAs current because the `# vN` comment is preserved.

controls.title: Generic credential and secret scanning
controls.gap: The PR-time TruffleHog job (verified secrets only, PR diff) landed in reference batch R3 but has not yet been proven on a real pull request with a seeded synthetic credential; the PII quarantine is deliberately not a generic token scanner.
controls.validation: Seed a synthetic detectable test credential on a throwaway branch, open a PR, and confirm the secret-scan job fails without printing the material; then flip to verified with the run number as evidence.
controls.notes: Keep PII and credential scanning as separate controls.

controls.title: Private vulnerability disclosure route
controls.gap: SECURITY.md is GitHub's placeholder boilerplate with fictional supported versions and no real private reporting channel.
controls.blocker: The owner must enable and test GitHub Private Vulnerability Reporting, or provide a monitored private security contact (docs/DECISIONS-NEEDED.md section 22).
controls.validation: An external non-collaborator can find and use the documented private route; the owner confirms receipt; SECURITY.md contains no placeholder or fictional information.
controls.notes: Never invent an email address or advertise a channel nobody monitors.

controls.title: Protected default branch and required checks
controls.gap: main is not protected: no PR requirement, no required checks, force-push and deletion allowed. The exact setting is written up in docs/DECISIONS-NEEDED.md section 23; it cannot be applied from inside the repository.
controls.validation: A read of the repository ruleset/branch protection proves the PR requirement, the required checks (pii-scan, lint, backend, postgres, frontend, frontend-e2e, docker-build), and force-push/delete protection.
controls.notes: Administration setting; reinforced by the Paperless, Twenty and Personal-Security-Checklist cycles.

controls.title: PII quarantine for repository content and history
controls.validation: The per-PR tree gate and the nightly full-history gate stay green; the scanner fails closed on a missing deny-list.
controls.notes: A verified PII control does not replace generic secret scanning (SEC-SC-002).

controls.title: GDPR erasure preview and execution
controls.validation: Tenant/admin authorization, preview/execute parity, legal-hold and statutory-retention behaviour stay covered by the privacy test suite.
controls.notes: Stronger than browser-local deletion because regulated records need classification and retention handling.

controls.title: JWT signing key separated from the application secret and rotatable in stages
controls.validation: New access tokens and OIDC state sign only with the active key (JWT_SIGNING_KEY, falling back to SECRET_KEY when unset); verification tries the active key then at most three verify-only fallbacks; production refuses the insecure default, duplicates and an active key listed as a fallback; tests prove a staged rotation keeps the server-side session revocation authoritative and that a retired fallback invalidates old state.
controls.notes: Reference integration R3 (Flask SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS lesson). Rotating SECRET_KEY still rotates the local KEK (SEC-KEK-001); this control means a JWT rotation no longer forces that.

controls.title: Independent production key-encryption key
controls.gap: With the default KEK_PROVIDER=local the KEK is derived from SECRET_KEY, so rotating the application secret destroys every sealed tenant secret; production does not yet require KEK_PROVIDER=env + KEK_KEY.
controls.validation: Provision an independent KEK (KEK_PROVIDER=env, KEK_KEY), run a rotation/recovery drill, then make the production validator refuse the local fallback.
controls.notes: Provision first; hard-failing before the key is available would create an outage. SEC-JWT-001 removed the most common reason to rotate SECRET_KEY.

controls.title: Customer portal capability-token hardening
controls.gap: Long-lived plaintext capability token with revocation but no expiry.
controls.validation: Owner decides the standing-link product contract; then hash-at-rest/expiry/regeneration tests as approved.
controls.notes: Product semantics must be decided before changing link lifetime.

controls.title: PR-time dependency vulnerability review
controls.gap: The dependency-review job (fail on moderate or higher) landed in reference batch R3 but has not yet run on a real pull request; pip-audit in the lint job covers Python only.
controls.validation: The job passes on an ordinary PR and blocks a controlled PR that adds a moderate-or-higher vulnerable dependency; then flip to verified with the run numbers as evidence.
controls.notes: Retain pip-audit and weekly Dependabot; requires the repository dependency graph (free on public repositories).

controls.title: Browser/API security headers
controls.validation: Header middleware tests cover CSP, HSTS effective-HTTPS behaviour, framing/content-type/referrer policies and safe Content-Disposition.
controls.notes: Defence in depth; TLS termination remains required.

controls.title: Connect-time outbound destination validation
controls.validation: Webhook POSTs go through a transport that resolves right before connecting, refuses the destination if any answer is non-public (loopback, link-local, private, multicast, reserved, 100.64/10, 64:ff9b::/96), pins the socket to one vetted address with the original Host and SNI, and follows no redirects; registration and connect share one predicate; tests cover rebinding, mixed answers and redirects.
controls.notes: Closed audit finding SEC-009 in reference batch R1 (Paperless-ngx and Twenty cycles).
